To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) novice ontology authors benefit from guidance about how to use the ontology authoring interface, and (ii) they also benefit from guidance about what to add to the ontology.

(i) domain experts benefit from intuitive tool support for ontology authoring, in particular guidance about the ontology engineering process and the syntactical capabilities and limitations of a CNL, and understandable error messages; (ii) providing feedback about the integration process of ontology authors’ input into an existing ontology helps domain experts to become aware of ontology defects, and (iii) analysing and describing ontology authoring in the context of dialogue analysis and discourse structure can help to better understand the ontology authoring processes of

(i) the use of controlled natural language can make ontology authorship more accessible to non-experts; (ii) ontology authors benefit from guidance and feedback during the ontology authoring processes; (iii) the use of dialogues can make ontology authorships more intuitive and (iv) the use of a framework to describe the discourse structure of dialogues can facilitate the analysis of the ontology authoring dialogue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
making ontology authoring more intuitive for domain experts by providing them with intelligent tool support.
making ontology authoring easier and more intuitive for domain experts by providing tool support that is based on the knowledge of the domain expert.
the design of a CNL-based ontology editing system that is intuitive to use for domain experts.

the main contribution of this PhD is to show that intelligent tool support can make ontology authorship more accessible to domain users by providing guidance about the ontology engineering process and the ontology authoring syntax, by providing intuitive feedback about the consequences of adding new ontological knowledge, by fostering awareness of the ontology authoring task and by enabling the ontology authoring tool to be used in the same way as a dialogue system.

the more tool support is provided for ontology authoring the more accessible it becomes for domain experts, and that this tool support should include (i) guidance about the ontology building process, (ii) guidance about the correct syntax of the CNL used to write ontologies and (iii) guidance about the logical consequences and potential defects of adding new ontology constructs.
intelligent tool support for CNL-based ontology engineering is beneficial to domain experts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a number of insights into the ontology authoring task and the tool support needed to facilitate the task.
the main challenge in ontology authoring using CNL is the integration of syntactical and semantic analysis of the author’s input.

the combination of controlled natural language and intelligent tool support can help novice ontology authors to author more complete ontologies, with fewer errors and more easily than using traditional ontology languages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
providing intelligent tool support for ontology authoring is beneficial for domain experts.
the combination of controlled natural language and intelligent tool support is a promising approach for ontology authoring.

intelligent tool support for CNL-based ontology authors is beneficial, but it is also necessary to provide guidance about the authoring process and the syntactic capabilities of the controlled language to make it easier for ontology authors to use.
